note: Reel 30: How Sure Are You? Script v5, after three fact-and-story reviews and two cold reads. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart). The officer is am_michael (audition, 10 Nov: no creak on either line); his last two lines are the same takes as his first two. Facts: docs/research.md.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You're the only witness. Again.
Watch his face.
This time, he's one of these six, and whoever you pick goes to prison.
Out of ten, how sure are you?
So? Which one?
Good. That's him.
He's a drawing, so he can't see what you picked.
So here's the answer.
It's number three.
Look at him, and now how sure are you it's him?
It isn't number three.
I made that up.
But he looked right, didn't he?
And whoever you picked is still going to prison.
If I hadn't asked you first, one good, and you'd swear you were this sure from the start.
In America, police told a real witness she'd picked the same man again.
In her own words, Bingo. I did it right.
It was the wrong man, and Ronald Cotton lost more than ten years.
lines.text_kokoro: It was the wrong man, and Ronald [Cotton](/kˈɑːtən/) lost more than ten years.

lines.text: I could tell you which one, but you'd believe me.
So? Which one?
Good. That's him.
